newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks slip, blue-chips seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks slip, blue-chips seen strong.

text.p: Greek shares ended lower in profit taking after a weak start on Monday with analysts expecting bank, cement and food and beverage shares to continue to perform well until the end of the year.
"There was profit taking on Monday after the recent climb which was expected after the bourse's upside move," said analyst Takis Niarchos at Hellenic American Securities.

He said he expected banks, cement companies and blue chips like Hellenic Bottling to continue to perform well with macro-economic indicators improving, but did not expect them to affect affect the market in the short-run.
The socialist government's tough 1997 budget passed parliament on Saturday.

The Athens general share index closed down 0.76 percent or 7.16 points lower at 931.04 from Friday's 938.20 close after opening at 938.64. Trading volume rose to 19.1 billion drachmas on volume of 12.7 million shares in active block trading.
Losers led gainers 123 to 81 with 29 issues unchanged on 233 traded.
Banks lost 1.04 percent, construction dropped 1.31 percent while small caps and investment shares rose by 0.18 percent and 0.40 percent, respectively. Industrials closed 0.61 percent lower.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 569.00-587.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended 30 drachmas lower at 4,255.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $8.10-$9.10. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 3,143-3,345 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
